key_insight: Training a language model via large-scale agentic reinforcement learning with hardware-in-the-loop feedback enables automated generation of CUDA kernels that close the gap with compiler-based systems. Iterative execution + reward from real performance metrics produces kernels optimized for real GPUs rather than just syntactic correctness.
problem_solved: Automates the difficult, hardware-specific task of writing high-performance CUDA kernels by making LLMs competitive with compiler-based optimizers and reducing reliance on expert manual tuning.
method: Agentic RL loop: the model proposes CUDA kernels, they are executed on real GPUs, runtime/profiling metrics are collected, and rewards drive policy updates.
Scalable training on diverse kernels and workloads with hardware-aware reward shaping and correctness checks to prioritize both performance and validity.
Iterative refinement and decomposition strategies (generate → test → repair) combined with curriculum/data-augmentation to generalize across GPU architectures and patterns.
impact: Enables practitioners to automatically produce high-performance GPU code without deep hardware expertise, accelerating model deployment and optimization workflows and reducing manual tuning time.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of the agentic RL loop (generate kernel → run on GPU → collect perf counters → compute reward → update model).
Bar/line chart comparing runtime or throughput: CUDA Agent vs baseline LLMs vs compiler systems (e.g., torch.compile).
Schematic showing hardware-in-the-loop feedback: GPU icons feeding profiling counters back into the model.
Pipeline overview: training data sources, model training cluster, test farm of GPUs, and deployment path.
paper_title: CUDA Agent: Large-Scale Agentic RL for High-Performance CUDA Kernel Generation
paper_authors: Weinan Dai, Hanlin Wu, Qiying Yu, Huan-ang Gao, Jiahao Li
